reason: E2 directly supports that LPBF's ultra-high cooling rates inhibit grain growth and segregation, and E3 shows LPBF improves yield strength in CoCrFeNi via fine grains and dislocations. However, no cited evidence addresses AlCrFeNiSi specifically, the effect of high scan speeds on cooling rates, or the claimed reduction in residual stress and defect formation, leaving several premises unsupported.
premises: LPBF achieves ultra-high cooling rates (103–108 K/s) that inhibit grain growth and segregation
Rapid solidification in LPBF reduces compositional segregation and residual stress accumulation
LPBF yields refined microstructures with enhanced mechanical properties compared to conventional processing
High scan speeds in LPBF can be optimized to maximize cooling rates and microstructural benefits
The benefits of LPBF observed in other HEAs (e.g., CoCrFeNi) are transferable to AlCrFeNiSi
